standard_prerequisites.use: Keeps the exact sequence exact after tensoring the second base change, which yields surjectivity of the map on cycles.

core_obligations: Take a free resolution of M and write both Tor groups as quotients of the kernels K' and K'' of the first maps after the two base changes (proof lines 24072-24080).
Write the exact sequence computing the first base change and tensor it with R''; flatness of the first base change keeps it exact (proof lines 24081-24091).
Read off that the induced map K' tensor R'' to K'' is surjective, which descends to the two Tor groups as claimed (proof lines 24092-24094).
proof_roadmap: Put both Tor groups into one comparison of free resolutions (proof lines 24071-24080).
Use flatness to keep the tensored sequence exact and conclude surjectivity (proof lines 24081-24095).
difficulty_reason: For ring maps R to R' to R'' and an R-module M whose first base change is flat over R', the lemma states that the natural map from Tor_1(M, R') tensor R'' to Tor_1(M, R'') is surjective (statement lines 24062-24069). The proof does not compute Tor with a resolution over R'': it takes one free resolution over R, identifies both Tor groups as quotients of the kernels after the two base changes, tensors the exact sequence for the first base change with R'', and uses flatness to keep it exact, which makes the map on kernels surjective (proof lines 24071-24095). Using a single resolution for both computations, so that the comparison becomes a map of kernels, is the content of the argument. H2.
